steps.beforeInstructorMessage: You’re the chip leader holding 22 facing a single open—this is a classic spot to leverage your stack by set‑mining correctly.
steps.question: With pocket deuces as the big stack versus one preflop raise, do you flat and take a flop, turn your hand into a bluff, or muck the small pair?

gradingSpecJson.responseIncorrect: There is a better line in this node.
gradingSpecJson.followUpContent: Small pairs like 22 are rarely thrilled to play big pots preflop, but they shine when you can see a cheap flop with deep stacks behind as the covering player. As chip leader versus a single open, calling allows you to set‑mine profitably: you’ll miss the flop most of the time and simply fold, but when you do flop a set you have the stack depth and positional leverage to win a large pot or apply serious pressure on later streets. Three‑betting preflop tends to fold out all the hands you dominate and isolate you against stronger ranges, turning 22 into a bluff catcher at best and killing the very implied odds you were trying to realize. The key is to be realistic about your plan: you’re not trying to "win with deuces" by showdown; you’re trying to win big the small fraction of the time you hit hard while losing small when you miss. With the right price and position, that tradeoff favours a flat call, not a hero raise, and over time this disciplined approach to set‑mining is a quiet but powerful edge.
